column2: Ephraim gathers at Sephina and challenges Jephthah's going without calling them; the threat is to burn his house, with no supplied with-you-in-it clause.
Jephthah's dispute, Ammon's severe humiliation of him, his appeal and Ephraim's failure to save remain; I and my people retains the mixed individual/collective expression.
Putting his life in his hand precedes the Lord's delivering Ammon into his hand; both hand images and the challenge about today's attack remain.
Jephthah gathers all Gilead's men; their victory follows the insult about escaped Ephraimites between Ephraim and Manasseh.
column3: The quoted Gilead is expanded to you Gileadites as collective address; attribution of they had said is contextual, not an explicit Greek ethnonym in that clause.

column2: Propose And they said instead of And if they said: the selected text narrates a plural answer, without an explicit conditional. End the response here with a full stop.
column3: The exchange remains plural throughout; no individual fugitive or singular reply is substituted from a familiar version.

column2: Capitalize They after the preceding unit's restored sentence boundary; retain Password for synthema, failure to speak that way, slaughter and forty-two thousand.
column3: Password renders the selected Greek word rather than importing a Hebrew shibboleth/sibboleth pair absent here; whether the command requests or quotes a password remains a translation question.

column2: Jephthah's six-year judgeship, death and burial in his city Gilead remain as selected; no different burial locality is inserted.
Esebon of Bethlehem follows Jephthah; the selected personal name remains distinct from familiar alternate forms.
Thirty sons, thirty daughters sent outside and thirty wives brought from outside remain distinct groups, followed by seven years of judging.
column3: Outside does not itself specify the precise kinship or geographic boundary of the marriage network.

column2: Esebon dies and is buried in Bethlehem; the narrative's site is retained.
Elon is Zebulunite and judges ten years after Esebon; both notices remain.
The selected death in Ailim and subsequent burial in Zebulun's land remain distinct, with the plural they buried preserved.
Labdon son of Sellem the Pirathonite succeeds Elon; the selected names are not normalized to another textual tradition.
Forty sons and thirty grandsons account for seventy mounts, and the eight-year judgeship follows; sons of his sons preserves the explicit genealogy.
column3: Young donkeys specifies the contextual sense of poloi, as in 10:4, rather than asserting the noun alone always means donkey.

column2: Labdon's full identification recurs at death and burial in Pirathon, Ephraim, Mount Lanak; the selected mountain name remains.
Renewed evil is marked by again, and the Lord gives Israel into foreign hands for forty years; the stated period is preserved.
Manoah is from Zorah and Dan; both barrenness and not bearing remain descriptions of his wife.
Behold introduces the messenger's recognition of barrenness followed by conception and a son; ordinary you addresses the woman.
The caution prohibits wine, sikera and anything unclean; the negative scope of pan is represented by anything, not everything as a single collective prohibition.
column3: Sikera remains a source-grounded drink term requiring a glossary explanation, not a silently modernized beverage.

column2: The second behold, iron on the head, sanctified Nazirite status from the womb and beginning Israel's deliverance remain; iron is not narrowed to razor.
The woman reports a very glorious messenger-like appearance, says she did ask his origin, and says he did not report his name; no negative is inserted before asked.
column3: Very glorious for epiphanes sphodra is provisional; conspicuous or awe-inspiring alternatives require lexical judgment.

column2: Her report repeats the pregnancy, drink and impurity commands and adds Nazirite status until death; the report is not shortened to the previous speech.
Manoah's prayer uses Thee and Thou didst for direct address to the Lord; enlighten remains the source image for instruction about the coming child.
column3: I beseech Thee expresses the petition formula en emoi rather than a literal in-me phrase; the supplicatory function is contextual.

column2: God listens and the messenger comes again while the woman sits in the field; Manoah's absence is explicit.
The woman's haste and running precede her behold-announcement; the man from that day has appeared, preserving the backward reference.
Manoah follows his wife and asks the man's identity; I am supplies the English copula for the messenger's ego reply, without claiming a divine-name formula.
The coming-to-pass of the word introduces questions about the child's rule and deeds; the two nouns remain distinct.
column3: Rule for krima is provisional: the precise norm, manner or ordained course meant here requires lexical and contextual review.

column2: The messenger tells Manoah that she must guard against all he told the woman; the female subject is contextual from the following prohibitions.
Products of the vine, wine, sikera and every unclean thing are excluded, and all commands are to be observed; no permitted vine product is supplied.
Manoah urges the messenger to stay and proposes preparing a goat before him; to stay makes the hospitality context explicit.
The messenger refuses the loaves even if urged and directs any whole burnt offering to the Lord; plural loaves and Manoah's lack of recognition remain.
column3: Though interprets the first conditional concessively; the future offering verb is rendered as instruction in this conditional response. Neither choice identifies the messenger as the Lord by itself.

column2: Manoah requests the name for future glorification when the word comes to pass; ordinary you avoids deciding disputed messenger identity through pronouns.
The name-question is answered by wonderful; no christological title, proper name or explanation is inserted into the messenger's reply.
The goat and sacrifice are offered on the rock; the repeated Lord and wonder-working description remain while the couple watch.
column3: Sacrifice renders thysia without narrowing it to grain offering from a parallel tradition; the exact offering type remains open.

column2: The flame ascends toward heaven and the messenger ascends in it; the couple watch and fall facedown on the ground.
The messenger does not appear again, and only then Manoah recognizes him as the Lord's messenger; the recognition remains temporally placed.
Manoah's surely-die assertion represents the emphatic death construction, with because we have seen God retained as his stated reason.
The wife's counterargument gives three consequences of a wish to kill: no accepted offerings, no enlightenment and no hearing made possible; all three negatives remain.
The woman bears and names Samson; the Lord blesses him and the child grows in the selected order.
The Lord's Spirit begins accompanying Samson at Dan's camp between Zorah and Eshtaol; accompany is not silently changed to stir or rush upon.
